pages.textMedium:
The White Whale was hungry. Not snack hungry. Not dinner hungry. Eat-a-whole-ship hungry. His belly growled so loudly that a crab ran off to hide.

He had hunted for food all day, and all he had found was one old boot. He tried it. It tasted like boot.
pages.textLong:
The White Whale was hungry. Not snack hungry. Not dinner hungry. Eat-a-whole-ship hungry. His belly growled so loudly that a crab ran off to hide.

He had hunted for food all day, and all he had found was one old boot. He tried it. It tasted like boot.

He tried a round grey rock that looked a bit like a bun. It tasted like rock.

He tried a mouthful of seaweed. It tasted like wet hair.

"Is there ANYTHING to eat in this ocean?" he groaned.

A snail on the sand slowly pulled his head inside his shell. Just to be safe.
pages.scene: Blue-green sea with seaweed. The White Whale has a clump of seaweed hanging out of his mouth and a thoroughly disgusted face. On the sand beside the old boot lies a round grey rock with one big bite mark in it. The orange-shelled snail is pulling back into its shell, only the eye-stalks still showing. The crab's two eyes peek over the top of his rock.

pages.textMedium:
Then his nose caught something. Sniff. Something warm. Sniff, sniff. Something DELICIOUS.

The smell curled through the water like a golden ribbon. The White Whale followed it, all the way into a dark, dark sea cave.

Was he scared of the dark? Maybe a tiny bit. But hungry beats scared.
pages.textLong:
Then his nose caught something. Sniff. Something warm. Sniff, sniff. Something DELICIOUS.

The smell curled through the water like a golden ribbon. The White Whale followed it, all the way into a dark, dark sea cave.

Was he scared of the dark? Maybe a tiny bit. But hungry beats scared.

pages.textMedium:
In the roof of the cave was a hole, and the smell poured out of it. The White Whale pressed his eye to the hole.

Trolls! A whole family! Papa Troll stirred a pot as big as a bathtub. Mama Troll chopped onions as big as footballs.
pages.textLong:
In the roof of the cave was a hole, and the smell poured out of it. The White Whale pressed his eye to the hole.

Trolls! A whole family! Papa Troll stirred a pot as big as a bathtub. Mama Troll chopped onions as big as footballs.

pages.textMedium:
The trolls were arguing. Trolls are always arguing.

"More salt," said Papa Troll.

"More onions," said Mama Troll.

"Salt!"

"Onions!"

Little Troll was supposed to lay the table. He was drumming on the bowls with two spoons instead.

Down below, the White Whale whispered one word. "Stew." His belly growled so hard the cave shook.
pages.textLong:

"More salt," said Papa Troll.

"More onions," said Mama Troll.

"Salt!"

"Onions!"

Little Troll was supposed to lay the table. He was drumming on the bowls with two spoons instead.

Down below, the White Whale whispered one word. "Stew." His belly growled so hard the cave shook.
pages.scene: The troll kitchen, cosy and firelit. Papa Troll and Mama Troll stand nose to nose over the giant steaming pot: he holds a huge salt pot, she holds an onion as big as a football. At the table Little Troll (small, round, mossy green-grey, big ears, one tooth, orange tuft of hair) drums happily on three bowls with two spoons. In the floor hole the White Whale's big eye stares at the pot. The mouse on the shelf covers its ears.

pages.textMedium:
So he had an idea: the straw. He pressed his lips to the hole and sucked as hard as a whale can suck. SHLOOOP!

Something shot down the hole and into his mouth. Stew? No. A wooden spoon. He tried it. It tasted like spoon.

"Who took my spoon?" roared Papa Troll.

"It wasn't me," said Little Troll.
pages.textLong:
First idea: the straw. He pressed his lips to the hole and sucked as hard as a whale can suck. SHLOOOP!

Something shot down the hole and into his mouth. Stew? No. A wooden spoon. He tried it. It tasted like spoon.

"Who took my spoon?" roared Papa Troll.

"It wasn't me," said Little Troll.
pages.scene: The dark sea cave below the kitchen. The White Whale floats just under the small glowing hole in the roof with a giant wooden spoon sticking out of his mouth like a lollipop, looking puzzled and let down. Steam drifts down from the hole. The little orange-and-white fish beside him is giggling behind a fin.

pages.textLong:
Second idea: the tongue. He poked his tongue up through the hole and felt around for the pot.

In the kitchen, a fat pink thing came wiggling across the floor.

"Slug!" said Mama Troll. She swept it back down the hole with her broom.

"Thath not nithe," said the White Whale.
pages.scene: The troll kitchen floor. The White Whale's big pink tongue pokes up out of the floor hole and feels its way toward the pot. Mama Troll stands over it with a broom, not impressed at all, about to sweep. Papa Troll stirs the pot with a huge fish bone because his spoon is gone. The mouse has jumped onto a stool in fright.

pages.textLong:
Third idea: make the hole bigger. He backed up, took aim, and rammed the roof with his head. BONK!

Up in the kitchen, the bowls jumped. An onion rolled off the table.

"Stop stomping!" said Mama Troll.

"It wasn't me!" said Little Troll.

Was the hole any bigger? No. But the whale's head was. He had a bump like an egg.
pages.scene: The sea cave. The White Whale floats just under the rocky roof with a round bump on his head as big as an egg, eyes dizzy, little stars circling him. A few pebbles sink past. The small glowing hole above is exactly as small as before. The little fish winces and the crab covers his eyes with both claws.

pages.textMedium:
It was no use. The hole was only as big as his eye, and you can't eat stew with your eye.

He needed another way in. So he swam round and round the cave, searching every crack. A little fish swam round behind him.

"What are we looking for?" asked the little fish.

"A door," said the White Whale.
pages.textLong:
It was no use. The hole was only as big as his eye, and you can't eat stew with your eye.

He needed another way in. So he swam round and round the cave, searching every crack. A little fish swam round behind him.

"What are we looking for?" asked the little fish.

"A door," said the White Whale.

There was no door. But on a rock sat a crab. The same crab as before. He had seen everything.

"There is one more hole," said the crab. "Over there, in the dark corner. But you do not want that hole."

"Why not?"

"You just don't."

Did the White Whale listen? Have you met him?
pages.scene: The dark sea cave. The crab sits on a rock and points one claw, very unwillingly, toward a far dark corner where a second shaft opens in the roof with a single thin green wisp curling out of it. His other claw is raised in warning. The White Whale is already turning toward the corner with a hopeful face. The little fish floats between them, looking worried.

pages.textMedium:
He found one more hole. Just one. He stuck his nose in... and yanked it right back out.

"EW!"

This hole did NOT smell like fish stew. This hole led straight up to the troll bathroom. Right under the troll toilet. Yep.
pages.textLong:
There it was. One more hole. Just one. He stuck his nose in... and yanked it right back out.

"EW!"

This hole did NOT smell like fish stew. This hole led straight up to the troll bathroom. Right under the troll toilet. Yep.

pages.textMedium:
The White Whale sank to the bottom of the cave. One hole too small. One hole too stinky. And a belly as empty as a drum.

The toughest whale in the ocean, going to bed with a boot for dinner?

"No," he said. He pinched his nose shut with one flipper and swam back to the stinky hole. Hungry beats stinky. Probably.
pages.textLong:

The toughest whale in the ocean, going to bed with a boot for dinner?

"No," he said. He pinched his nose shut with one flipper and swam back to the stinky hole. Hungry beats stinky. Probably.
pages.scene: The floor of the sea cave. The White Whale lies flat on the sand with his chin down, glum, rumble lines at his empty belly. Far behind him the warm yellow beam from the kitchen hole shines down; in the other corner a green wisp hangs under the second hole. The crab kindly holds out a small bunch of seaweed to him. The little fish pats his cheek with a fin.

pages.textLong:
Up in the kitchen, the stew was nearly done. Papa Troll had put in the salt. Mama Troll had put in the onions. Now they were arguing about pepper.

"Little Troll! Wash your hands! Dinner!"

"I have to GO first," said Little Troll.

"Now? You always have to go when it's time to lay the table."

But he was already gone.
pages.scene: The troll kitchen. The table is half laid with bowls and the giant pot steams over the fire. Mama Troll points sternly at a wash bucket; Papa Troll holds a big pepper pot over the stew. Little Troll is hurrying out through the doorway with his knees pressed together, hopping from foot to foot. Behind everyone's back the mouse drags away a crust of bread.

pages.textMedium:
Up above, Little Troll came stomping in. "Nobody come in!" he shouted. "I need to concentrate!"

He sat down. He scrunched up his face. He went as red as a tomato. And then —

PLOP. PLOP. PLOP-PLOP.
pages.textLong:
Up above, Little Troll came stomping in. "Nobody come in!" he shouted. "I need to concentrate!"

He sat down. He scrunched up his face. He went as red as a tomato. And then —

PLOP. PLOP. PLOP-PLOP.

pages.textMedium:
The smell rolled down the hole like green fog. It was the worst smell in the history of smells. The White Whale crossed his eyes. He stuck out his tongue.

"Blearrgh! Ooof! Hnnngh!"

He made faces nobody had ever made before. And deep in his nose, a tickle began.
pages.textLong:
The smell rolled down the hole like green fog. It was the worst smell in the history of smells. The White Whale crossed his eyes. He stuck out his tongue.

"Blearrgh! Ooof! Hnnngh!"

He made faces nobody had ever made before. And deep in his nose, a tickle began.

pages.textMedium:
The tickle got bigger. He pulled a face like a squashed plum. He pulled a face like a surprised potato.

"Hnnk! Fffp! Gnnnrrrgh!"

The crab and the little fish tried to copy the faces. They couldn't. Nobody could.

He clamped both flippers over his nose. He held on. He held on. He held —
pages.textLong:

The crab and the little fish tried to copy the faces. They couldn't. Nobody could.

He clamped both flippers over his nose. He held on. He held on. He held —
pages.scene: The sea cave under the second hole, thin green fog all around. The White Whale clamps both flippers over his nose, cheeks blown up like balloons, one eye huge and the other squeezed tiny. Next to him the crab and the little fish pull their own silly faces, trying to copy him: the crab cross-eyed with his claws by his cheeks, the fish with its tongue out.

pages.textMedium:
"Ah... ah... AH-CHOOOO!"

The sneeze shot straight up the hole. WHOOSH went the toilet! Little Troll flew off his seat, toilet rolls and all, and a brown, whirling, twirling POOP TORNADO went spinning through the whole troll cave.
pages.textLong:
"Ah... ah... AH-CHOOOO!"

The sneeze shot straight up the hole. WHOOSH went the toilet! Little Troll flew off his seat, toilet rolls and all, and a brown, whirling, twirling POOP TORNADO went spinning through the whole troll cave.

pages.textMedium:
Out of the bathroom it spun and down the hall. It took the toilet rolls. It took the bath mat. It took Papa Troll's enormous underpants right off the washing line.

Round and round on top rode Little Troll, hugging his rubber duck.

Was he scared? A bit. Was it the best day of his life? Also yes.
pages.textLong:
Out of the bathroom it spun and down the hall. It took the toilet rolls. It took the bath mat. It took Papa Troll's enormous underpants right off the washing line.

Round and round on top rode Little Troll, hugging his rubber duck.

Was he scared? A bit. Was it the best day of his life? Also yes.
pages.scene: A new place: the troll hallway, a rocky cave corridor with a washing line strung across it. The cheerful brown cartoon tornado swirl spins down the hall trailing streamers of toilet paper, with a huge pair of spotted troll underpants flapping in it. Little Troll rides round on top hugging the rubber duck, half terrified and half grinning. The little spider clings to its thread, blown out sideways. Nothing rude is shown.

pages.textMedium:
Down in the sea cave, the White Whale heard it all. Crash! Clatter! An awful lot of yelling.

Most whales would have swum away. But this whale had one thought in his head, and the thought was: STEW.

He shot across the cave, stopped right under the kitchen hole, and opened his mouth as wide as it would go.
pages.textLong:

He shot across the cave, stopped right under the kitchen hole, and opened his mouth as wide as it would go.
pages.scene: The sea cave. The White Whale is parked directly under the warm glowing kitchen hole with his mouth open enormously wide, eyes squeezed shut, full of hope. Dust and crumbs shake down from the trembling hole above. Behind a rock the crab and the little fish peek out; the little fish has opened its own tiny mouth wide too, just in case.

pages.textMedium:
"RUN!" yelled Papa Troll. "MY HAIR!" yelled Mama Troll.

The tornado spun through the kitchen, grabbed the giant pot of fish stew, and tipped it down the hole in the floor — SPLOSH — straight into the wide-open mouth of the White Whale.
pages.textLong:
"RUN!" yelled Papa Troll. "MY HAIR!" yelled Mama Troll.

The tornado spun through the kitchen, grabbed the giant pot of fish stew, and tipped it down the hole in the floor — SPLOSH — straight into the wide-open mouth of the White Whale.

The stew kept coming. So did the rest of the kitchen. An onion as big as a football. A ladle. A pepper pot.

He spat out the ladle. He knew what that would taste like. And he was very, very careful with the pepper. One sneeze was enough for today.

The crab and the little fish caught the splashes.
pages.scene: The sea cave under the kitchen hole. The White Whale, cheeks bulging and a stew-orange smile around his mouth, spits a big ladle out to one side and nudges a troll pepper pot away very carefully with one flipper. The last of the stew pours down from the hole. The little fish gobbles a floating piece of carrot and the crab catches drips in an empty shell held up like a bowl.

pages.textMedium:
Gulp. "Delicious," said the White Whale.

Up in the cave, the trolls got out their mops. "It wasn't me," said Little Troll. Nobody believed him.

Far away, the White Whale drifted home with a full, warm belly. He burped one small, happy burp, and fell asleep. Because even the toughest whale in the ocean has to sleep sometime.
